story: A Slocum glider running WHOI's LFDCS classifier has been listening for marine mammals in the Chukchi Sea off northwest Alaska since July 24, 2026, publishing analyst reviewed detections that include an air gun class

claims.claim: A Slocum G2 glider was deployed in the Chukchi Sea off the northwest coast of Alaska on July 24, 2026.
claims.verbatim: A Slocum G2 glider was deployed in the Chukchi Sea off the northwest coast of Alaska on July 24, 2026 to study the occurrence of several species of marine mammals
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring project page for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Read twice on separate fetches of the deployment landing page. This is the operator's own page, not reporting.

claims.claim: The glider is listed as an active mission under the designation unit 595 on the Robots4Whales site.
claims.verbatim: Slocum Glider G2, Chukchi Sea, Northwestern Alaska (Arctic)
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: The mission list names the Chukchi Sea deployment as active. The unit number appears in the URL path and page title of the detail pages at dcs.whoi.edu, which were fetched separately.

claims.claim: The deployment page's daily detection grid carries eight sound classes.
claims.verbatim: Fin whale Beluga whale Killer whale Bearded seal Bowhead whale Walrus Air gun Other
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring project page for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Verbatim string is the grid's class headings read in the page's own left to right order across two independent fetches, which agreed on both the count and the order. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the brief handed to me. Eight classes is six animal categories plus Air gun plus Other, NOT seven animals plus air gun. Do not write that seven are animals. SHOWRUNNER RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-29 on an independent fetch: 8 headings, order confirmed, Killer whale present.

claims.claim: Killer whale is the third class named in the deployment page's detection grid.
claims.verbatim: Killer whale
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring project page for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Confirmed on two independent fetches of the landing page. Read C05 before using, because the near real time detection table does NOT carry this column.

claims.claim: The near real time detection table for the deployment carries seven sound class columns and has no Killer whale column.
claims.verbatim: Date/time / Fin whale / Beluga whale / Bearded seal / Bowhead whale / Walrus / Air gun / Other / Duration / Tracks / Reviewed / Map / Latitude / Longitude
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Three independent fetches of this table returned the same header row with no Killer whale column. This is a real discrepancy with the landing page grid, verified in both directions, and the deck should say eight classes on the project page while the detection table publishes seven. Do not blend the two counts. SHOWRUNNER RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-29 on an independent fetch: header row transcribed as Date/time, Fin whale, Beluga whale, Bearded seal, Bowhead whale, Walrus, Air gun, Other, Duration, Tracks, Reviewed, Map, Latitude, Longitude. 7 sound-class columns, no Killer whale.

claims.claim: Air gun is one of the sound classes the system tallies alongside the animal classes.
claims.verbatim: Air gun
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Appears as a column heading on both the landing grid and the detection table. NEEDS SOFTENING if glossed. No fetched page defines Air gun as seismic survey noise, so write it as the page writes it, or hedge with 'air guns are the sound source used in marine seismic surveying' only if a separate source is added.

claims.claim: The Other class is defined as everything the call library does not contain.
claims.verbatim: Other indicates all calls/sounds not found in the call library
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Footnote under the detection table. Confirmed on the first full transcription fetch.

claims.claim: Tallies of classified calls are reported by the DMON every 15 minutes.
claims.verbatim: Tallies of classified calls are reported by the DMON every 15 minutes
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Table footnote, quoted exactly as the scout reported it. Corroborated by the 15 minute spacing of the timestamps in the table body.

claims.claim: Only calls averaging 11 dB above background or higher are tallied and reported as pitch tracks.
claims.verbatim: Only calls with an average amplitude of 11 dB above background or higher are tallied and reported as pitch tracks
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Table footnote. The scout's 11 dB figure holds.

claims.claim: Only calls with a Mahalanobis distance under 3 are tallied.
claims.verbatim: Only calls with a Mahalanobis distance less than 3 are tallied
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Table footnote. This is the classifier's confidence gate and pairs naturally with C09 on a slide about how strict the machine is.

claims.claim: Pitch tracks of individual calls are reported at a maximum rate of 8 KB per hour.
claims.verbatim: Pitch tracks of individual calls are reported at a maximum rate of 8 KB per hour
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Table footnote. Sanity check passes, 8 KB per hour is a plausible Iridium satellite budget and explains the next footnote about not every detected call being sent home.

claims.claim: Not every call the system detects is sent back as a pitch track.
claims.verbatim: While all detected calls are tallied in the table above, they are not all reported as pitch tracks
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring detection table for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Table footnote. Useful honesty beat, the bandwidth limit shapes what a human ever gets to check.

claims.claim: All dates and times published in the detection table are in the AKDT time zone.
claims.verbatim: All dates/times in AKDT time zone

claims.notes: Table footnote. Any timestamp the deck prints is Alaska local time and should be labelled that way.

claims.notes: Two independent fetches of the landing page both counted 36 dated links running 07/24/2026 to 08/28/2026. Arithmetic agrees, 8 days in July plus 28 in August is 36. The verbatim is the most recent date link, since a count is not a string on the page. NEEDS SOFTENING on 'consecutive', which I did not verify link by link.

claims.notes: Say 'the latest published record is dated August 28th', not 'the glider is still on station'. No fetched page states the glider's operational status, and a page can lag a recovery.

claims.notes: The page names the reviewer but does not state a review frequency, so do not write 'reviews daily'. The scout's 'daily' was a paraphrase and is killed below.

claims.claim: The Alaska Ocean Observing System supported development of the Arctic marine mammal call library and the preparation and operation of the glider in 2026.
claims.verbatim: Support for the development of the Arctic marine mammal call library as well as the preparation and operation of the glider in 2026 was provided by the Alaska Ocean Observing System.
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring project page for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: The call library is the thing the classifier compares against, so this is the funder of the machine's vocabulary.

claims.claim: The glider itself was procured in 2016 with support from the North Pacific Research Board.
claims.verbatim: The glider was procured in 2016 with support from the North Pacific Research Board.
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Digital Acoustic Monitoring project page for chukchi2607 unit 595
claims.notes: Sanity check passes, a 2016 hull carrying a 2026 classifier is a coherent and useful contrast for the deck.

claims.claim: DMON stands for digital acoustic monitoring instrument and is a passive acoustic instrument developed at Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution that records and processes audio in real time.
claims.verbatim: the digital acoustic monitoring instrument or DMON, a passive acoustic instrument developed at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution that is capable of recording and processing audio in real time
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: dcs.whoi.edu root returned no readable body to this fetcher, so the definition comes from WHOI's own Robots4Whales explainer, which is still the operator's page. No dated byline on the explainer, so treat it as background rather than news.

claims.claim: LFDCS stands for low frequency detection and classification system and runs on the DMON to identify marine mammal calls.
claims.verbatim: We have implemented a low-frequency detection and classification system (LFDCS; Baumgartner and Mussoline 2011) on the DMON to identify marine mammal calls from a variety of autonomous platforms.
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: The page dates the method to Baumgartner and Mussoline 2011, which is worth saying, this is not a new model.

claims.claim: The classifier extracts simple statistics from each pitch track and uses discriminant function analysis to classify each call.
claims.verbatim: extracts simple statistics of each pitch track (e.g., duration, average frequency, rate of change of frequency with time) and uses discriminant function analysis to classify each call
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: Load bearing for honesty. This is classical statistical pattern recognition, not a neural network, and the deck should not call it deep learning.

claims.claim: The classifier compares calls against a known call library defined before the instrument is deployed.
claims.verbatim: a known set of calls contained in a call library that is defined prior to deployment of the DMON/LFDCS
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: Pairs with C07. The library is fixed at launch, which is exactly why an unlisted code like Mn ends up in a human's note instead of a column.

claims.claim: Pitch tracks are evaluated by a human analyst to decide whether whale calls are really present.
claims.verbatim: the pitch tracks are evaluated by a human analyst to determine whether there are really whale calls present or not
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: The human in the loop beat, sourced to the operator rather than asserted.

claims.claim: The robots detect sounds, identify the species from the characteristics of those sounds and report to researchers on shore by satellite in near real time.
claims.verbatim: automatically detect those sounds, identify the species based on characteristics of the sounds, and report which species have been heard to researchers on shore via satellite in near real time
claims.source_outlet: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, Robots4Whales
claims.notes: Operator's own description of the pipeline.

killed.claim: Seven of the eight detection classes are animals and one is the air gun.
killed.why: Arithmetic is wrong and the scout's framing does not survive the page. The eight classes are fin whale, beluga whale, killer whale, bearded seal, bowhead whale and walrus, which is six animal categories, plus Air gun and plus Other. Six animals, one industrial source, one catch all. See C03.

killed.claim: Mn in the analyst notes means the humpback whale, Megaptera novaeangliae.
killed.why: No fetched page defines the code. The deployment page, the detection table, the notes page and the Robots4Whales explainer were all read and none expands Mn. The species reading is standard cetacean shorthand but it is inference, not a sourced fact. Print the code, per C30.

killed.claim: Walrus are a subsistence species for northwest Alaska communities.
killed.why: Could not source it. fws.gov/program/marine-mammals-management/subsistence-use and fws.gov/office/alaska-marine-mammals-management both returned HTTP 404. The FWS Pacific walrus species page contains no subsistence sentence. The Kawerak Eskimo Walrus Commission page returned truncated content with no usable text. ADF&G's walrus page names 'Alaska Native hunters' only in a predator list, which does not support the claim. Bowhead, beluga and bearded seal survive as C40 to C42, so write about those three and leave walrus out.

The FAA BEYOND program page was last updated May 13, 2025 and carries no deadline. A sam.gov search URL returned only the page chrome with no opportunity content. Single sourced to a trade outlet the brief itself flagged, so it dies.
